leo_docs: heads up — we got a post in community about the "function caller" examples being inconsistent across SDKs. link to thread: https://community.redwood.ai/t/buggy-caller-examples
tara_devex: thanks — can you paste the snippet folks are hitting?
leo_docs: gist: `resp = client.call_tool('summarize', input); print(resp)` — users expect parsed output but this shows raw envelope and leads to support tickets
ivan_sdk: hmm that's on us. our python quickstart used the thin envelope example; js used `const out = await parseWithSchema(res)` which made the docs diverge. i'll align them.
oscar_ml: another issue: guardrail example shows `additionalProperties: false` but then the tool returns a union string/object in examples. it confuses parsers when the LLM emits a bare string. we should explicitly show `oneOf` + a small shim to normalize
sre-bot: CI note: docs-link-check reported 2 dead anchors in /docs/migration/function-calling.md
leo_docs: i'll PR a patch — plan: 1) fix python and js snippets to both call `unwrap_envelope(resp)` helper 2) add a tiny shim for union returns: `if isinstance(x, str): x = json.loads(x)` (py) and `if (typeof x === 'string') x = JSON.parse(x)` (js) 3) add a short FAQ entry about 'null vs absent tool outputs' (show both examples)
tara_devex: also please include a streaming snippet for JS that demonstrates `for await (const chunk of stream)` — we've had people forget `await` and hit runtime errors
ivan_sdk: will add that. also propose adding a short test in docs repo that runs the python snippet with a mocked response so we catch regressions
oscar_ml: for the schema, suggest we show two variants under 'guardrails': minimal strict object and permissive union. e.g., `oneOf: [ {type: 'object', properties: {answer: {type: 'string'}}}, {type: 'string'} ]` and then show the normalization step.
leo_docs: good. also will add example showing `parse_with_schema(..., allow_array=True)` vs single object, because we've seen people accidentally wrap results differently between models
sre-bot: lint: heading levels inconsistent in the migration guide (line 134) — small fix noted
ivan_sdk: i'll open PR 678 to align snippets and add tests. tagging @tara_devex for review
tara_devex: please make the FAQ entry concrete: title 'Tool outputs: absent vs null vs envelope' with 3 quick bullets and copyable snippets. keep it short
oscar_ml: quick note for wording — prefer 'nullable' when schema allows explicit null. add a one-liner explaining omission vs null field semantics
leo_docs: pushing draft now, includes new helper `def unwrap_envelope(resp): return resp.get('output') if 'output' in resp else resp` and JS equivalent `function unwrapEnvelope(resp){ return resp.output ?? resp }`
ivan_sdk: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/678 — includes tests, link fixes, and a small example harness using `pytest`
leo_docs: great — can someone add a tiny section in migration guide 'Quick debugging checklist' with 4 items: check envelope, check schema type, try parse_with_schema(allow_array=True), verify streaming await
tara_devex: i'll add that after this merges. LGTM on examples, please add short unit test names and I'll approve
sre-bot: linkcheck green after PR 678 changes
ivan_sdk: reviewers approved, merging in 2
leo_docs: merged. filing follow-up issue to track adding these snippets in the SDK cookbooks across languages
leo_docs: thanks team — should reduce the duplicate support requests :tada:
